themes.name: AI boom or bubble?
themes.what: Huge spending on AI chips and data centres has driven US tech to records. Bubbles usually burst when that spending slows or interest rates bite, not when people first start worrying.
themes.bull: AI spending keeps rising: chip makers, data-centre power and cooling, and Indian firms building AI services gain.
themes.bear: Spending pauses or returns disappoint: US tech can fall 20–40%, global risk-off hits Indian IT and high-valuation stocks first.

themes.name: US rates & dollar liquidity (repo)
themes.what: When US yields rise or dollar liquidity tightens (repo rates spiking above the Fed’s rate, reverse-repo cushion drained), foreign money leaves emerging markets like India.
themes.bull: Yields fall and liquidity is plentiful: foreign investors buy Indian banks and large caps, and the rupee steadies.
themes.bear: Yields jump or repo stress appears: foreign selling, weaker rupee, rate-sensitive sectors fall.

themes.name: Gold cycle
themes.what: Gold rises when real interest rates fall, the dollar weakens, or fear rises (wars, central-bank buying). Jewellers and gold-loan lenders ride it.
themes.bull: Gold keeps climbing: jewellers’ inventory gains boost profits (part of the TBZ story), and gold-loan NBFCs grow faster.
themes.bear: Gold corrects after a big run: jeweller stocks often fall 2–3× harder than gold itself.

themes.name: Crude oil
themes.what: India imports most of its oil. Expensive crude raises inflation, widens the trade deficit and hurts companies that use oil as raw material.
themes.bull: Crude falls: oil marketers, paints, tyres, airlines and chemicals gain; the rupee and inflation improve.
themes.bear: Crude spikes (e.g. Middle East conflict): OMCs, paints and airlines fall; ONGC and Oil India gain.

themes.name: Dollar vs rupee
themes.what: A weaker rupee helps exporters (IT, pharma, textiles) earn more rupees, but raises import costs and scares foreign investors.
themes.bull: Rupee weakens gradually: exporters’ margins improve.
themes.bear: Rupee falls sharply: foreign selling, imported inflation, RBI may tighten.

themes.name: India capex & power
themes.what: Government and private spending on roads, railways, power grids and factories. Power demand is also rising with data centres and EVs.
themes.bull: Order books keep growing: capital goods, power equipment and cables re-rate.
themes.bear: Spending slows (elections, fiscal squeeze) or valuations are already stretched: sharp corrections.

g.k: Basket of LT, SIEMENS, ABB, BHEL…

themes.name: Defence & make-in-India
themes.what: Record defence budgets and export orders. These stocks run hard on order news, then cool for long stretches.
themes.bull: New big orders and exports: steady long-term growth.
themes.bear: Valuations far ahead of earnings: 30–50% drawdowns have happened even in strong years.

g.k: Basket of HAL, BEL, BDL, MAZDOCK…

themes.name: Market fear gauge
themes.what: India VIX and US VIX measure expected volatility. Low readings mean calm, sometimes complacent, markets; spikes mean panic, which is often when long-term bargains appear.
themes.bull: VIX low and steady: trends tend to continue.
themes.bear: VIX spiking: expect wide swings; reduce leverage and buy only in parts.
